items.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024
items.q: the first time you heard J.J. Johnson and then in a live situation with Ed Pratt’s band.

ctx.x: Yup, yup, And all those musicians, the ones that are still alive are still my best friends. You know? All of them. All of them. I loved all of them and their children talk about me. Most of them are gone you know but their kids, like for instance Joe Morris’s son has a band. He plays the drums. He just hired me to be at his music festival in Pensacola, Florida on December 1. He hired me. And he said that he thanks me and the other musicians that were his father’s friends you know, for his ability to play music.…

There’s a term you used a couple of times, you were talking about the first time you heard J.J. Johnson and then in a live situation with Ed Pratt’s band. And you were listening to these players and you said, “I was wrecked.” And I was thinking, well some people the reaction they would have had would be to give up. To say no way, no way am I ever going to do that so I’ll find something else to do. But you chose not to give up.

And I didn’t give up and I haven’t given up yet. J.J., I heard J.J. play a tune, one of his tunes, called “Overdrive.” I still can’t play it. But the way he played it so fluently and so fluidly. He was — the way he approached those changes — I still cannot do it the way he did it. And I have tried, I tried to record that tune and it’s not anything the way J.J. does it. You know so, and I can’t say if he got it naturally or maybe he learned how to play © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
